## [0.25.0](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/compare/v0.24.0...v0.25.0) (2026-11-17)

## Key Changes

Version 0.25.0 removes the beta Runloop sandbox provider and changes how Pydantic run contexts are checkpointed. Runloop users should preserve their workspace data before switching providers. Applications that share checkpoints across workers should upgrade readers first.

### Highlights:

- Migrate Runloop workloads to another supported sandbox provider, such as Modal, or remain on 0.24.0 while migrating. Provider-specific sessions and snapshots require a separate data migration.
- Resume nested agent-tool approvals with output guardrails using RunState schema `1.22`. Pydantic checkpoints now preserve default values and in-place edits. Use a custom serializer for process-local resources.
- `OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession` now defaults to `gpt-6-luna`. Set `model="gpt-4.1"` to keep the previous choice. Agent model settings also follow the selected model more closely. Native Chat Completions tool requests for `gpt-6-sol` and `gpt-6-luna` default to non-reasoning mode when no effort is supplied.
- Runner handoffs can opt into recovery with `failure_error_function`. Omitting it preserves exception propagation. The demo REPL can now approve or reject individual tool calls.
- MCP v2 Streamable HTTP supports concurrent requests. MCP v1 retains serialized requests. Failed and incomplete Responses calls now retain provider-reported token usage.

### Features

* expose utilities for third-party session adapters ([#5428](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/issues/5428)) ([16fdb20](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/commit/16fdb2091d0b18cc1200d26ba6a20ee6f1962455))
* **sandbox:** remove Runloop provider ([#5369](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/issues/5369)) ([12ce34d](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/commit/12ce34d8438d6f1f7c964a261b89e069e8a0b3d3))


### Bug Fixes

* avoid loading workspace startup files during internal sandbox operations ([#5406](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/pull/5406)) ([841dfdd](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/commit/841dfdd938bfd4ca052475eb76d6245a356868e0))
* preserve nested ToolContext approval decisions across resume ([#5633](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/pull/5633)) ([c200ae8](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/commit/c200ae8bd5b3f7510f0893f467aa9d118fdc7b12))

title: openai/openai-agents-python v1.0.0-alpha.1 — Agents SDK v1.0.0-alpha.1
body:
# Agents SDK v1.0.0-alpha.1

This first preview from `feat/simple-codex` adds Codex as an opt-in model provider for the Python Agents SDK. The prebuilt `openai-agents` wheels (version `1.0.0a1`) are available exclusively through GitHub Releases.

## Highlights

- **Choose Codex per run.** Import `CodexProvider` from `agents.models.codex` and create `provider = CodexProvider()`. Pass `RunConfig(model_provider=provider)` to the Runner. Codex uses your saved login. For API key authentication, use `CodexProvider(api_key=...)`. The provider selects the model for agents that use a model name or the default model. [Run the same agent with either provider](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/87e8f533c3b457fe632a5eb38ac42590d7f4d9fc/docs/models/codex.md#run-one-agent-with-either-provider)
- **Reuse Codex Core inside Python.** The wheel embeds unmodified Codex Core `rust-v0.166.0` through PyO3. Direct calls to Core eliminate `codex app-server` startup and JSON-RPC. Reuse the provider to share one `ThreadManager` across calls. Each call gets a fresh thread. Use an SDK session for history and close the provider with `await provider.aclose()` when you finish. [Thread lifetime and history](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/87e8f533c3b457fe632a5eb38ac42590d7f4d9fc/docs/models/codex.md#streaming-history-and-cancellation) · [Codex source](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/6ff1e1ca3b30fc8b914720681fcf5fe62e95f856)
- **Use SDK tools and approvals.** Stream text, hand off to a specialist, pause for approval before a Python tool runs, and validate typed output. Native commands follow Codex's sandbox and approval settings. A native approval prompt ends the model call. [Execution and approvals](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/87e8f533c3b457fe632a5eb38ac42590d7f4d9fc/docs/models/codex.md#configure-execution) · [Supported tools and model settings](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/87e8f533c3b457fe632a5eb38ac42590d7f4d9fc/docs/models/codex.md#supported-features-and-limits)

## Install and try it

Activate a virtual environment with standard CPython 3.10–3.14. Copy the link for your platform and replace `WHEEL_URL` in the command below. Each link includes the SHA-256 digest that pip checks when it downloads the wheel. [Checksums for all four wheels](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/releases/download/v1.0.0-alpha.1/SHA256SUMS)

[Linux x86-64 (glibc 2.28+)](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/releases/download/v1.0.0-alpha.1/openai_agents-1.0.0a1-cp310-abi3-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl#sha256=bfc5db104b0bb36d7119c8fb3f1d2831b6b8b7d95b63b09b2162bb721433057d) · [Linux ARM64 (glibc 2.28+)](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/releases/download/v1.0.0-alpha.1/openai_agents-1.0.0a1-cp310-abi3-manylinux_2_28_aarch64.whl#sha256=8a776dccb6baa8c197c090305138818bb70411fa34706c128cca8e1acb080e15) · [macOS 11+ on Apple silicon](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/relea

# Agents SDK v0.24.0-alpha.8

## Highlights

- **Approve Python tool calls before they run.** Review the arguments and approve or reject the call. You can remember a decision for the rest of the Session. [Managed approval example](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/examples/codex/managed_approvals/README.md#inspect-and-decide)
- **Connect your own model client.** The native tool loop works with async Responses and Chat Completions clients, LiteLLM, AnyLLM, and custom adapters. [Application-owned model clients](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/docs/sdk/models.md#use-an-application-owned-model-client)
- **Add Realtime voice to a Session.** Use a server WebSocket, connect a browser over WebRTC, or attach to an existing SIP call. [Realtime connection options](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/examples/codex/native_voice.md#choose-a-connection)
- **Resume more kinds of work.** Save supported pending tool requests and approvals. Request and token budgets keep the usage already spent when you restore a supported checkpoint. [Restore a checkpoint with a budget](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/examples/codex/budgeted-recovery.md)
- **Install on more Linux systems.** The preview adds an ARM64 wheel. Both Linux wheels support glibc 2.28 or newer. [Preview wheel platform requirements](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/.github/RELEASING.md#L44)

## Added

- Observe tool-search calls, tool-search results, and hosted MCP approval decisions through `ModelOutputItemCompleted`. Use `include_execution_details=True` to receive full items; receive summaries by default. [Live tool observations](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e/packages/codex/src/_agents_codex/observation.py#L238-L267)

- Handle managed function approvals with `FunctionToolApprovalRequest` and `FunctionToolApprovalDecision`. Set `run_input_policy_before_approval=True` to run the input policy before the approval predicate as well as before execution. Return `FinishTurn(output)` from `tool_batch_completion` to propose a final value with output validation and completion checks. title: agno-agi/agno v3.2.1 — v3.2.1
body:
# Changelog

## New Features:
- **Session Compactions**: `GET /sessions/{session_id}/compactions` lists a session's compactions on `SqliteDb` and `PostgresDb`, newest first, with how many messages each replaced and the token count before and after.
- **Company Files**: A Task's files and the shared notes can now be read over the API with `GET /company/tasks/{task_id}/files` and `GET /company/notes`, each with a `/{path}` route to read one file. See [cookbook](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/main/cookbook/05_agent_os/30_company/16_company_file_tree.py).

## Improvements:
- **LinearTools, DiscordTools and ModelsLabTools**: Now take a `timeout` (default 30 seconds, 120 for ModelsLab) that applies to every request.
- **ExaTools**: Now takes `include_text`, `exclude_text`, `user_location`, `moderation`, `highlights` and `subpages`.
- **MCPTools**: `connect()` now returns `True` when connected and `False` when not.
- **Qdrant**: `async_insert` now takes `batch_size`, like `insert`.
- **WebSearchTools and DuckDuckGoTools**: Search errors now come back as a JSON result.
- **Skills**: Skill instructions, references and script output in Chinese and other non-ASCII languages now reach the model as readable characters.
- **AntigravityTools and AntigravityAgent**: Now default to `antigravity-preview-09-2026`.
- **Slack**: `default_role` gives Slack members not in `users=` the permissions of a managed role. Each member is still recorded as themselves.

## Bug Fixes:
- **SQLTools**: A `db_engine` you pass in is now always used, even when connection fields are also given, and `run_sql_query` now returns the database error when reading the result rows fails.
- **OpenRouter, Perplexity and Requesty**: Responses now use the model's own output limit when `max_tokens` is not set, so long answers come back complete.
- **OpenRouterResponses**: Run and message metrics now include the `cost` that OpenRouter reports for each request.
- **Traces**: `GET /traces` now counts pages from 1, like the other trace routes, and `JsonDb` and `GcsJsonDb` apply `limit` when no `page` is given.
- **WebSearchTools and DuckDuckGoTools**: `max_results=0` now returns no results, and `search_news` applies the `modifier`.
- **ExaTools**: `livecrawl` now reaches Exa, and Exa's summaries and highlights now reach the model.
- **PostgresDb**: If creating a table fails on `PostgresDb` or `AsyncPostgresDb`, the same db instance now creates it on the next call once the cause is fixed.
- **MCPTools**: A failed or cancelled `connect()` now closes the connection and any stdio server it started.
- **Qdrant**: `insert(batch_size=...)` now sends documents in batches of that size.
- **CodexAgent**: Native permission requests and questions now work with `openai-codex` 0.163.0 and newer.
- **DaytonaTools**: `agno[daytona]` now installs a Daytona SDK that `DaytonaTools` supports (`daytona<1`), and the import error names that version.
- **Mistral**: `agno[mistral]` now skips

body:
## [2.15.0](https://github.com/google/adk-python/compare/v2.14.1...v2.15.0) (2026-11-19)

### Highlights

This release keeps voice streams and agent turns responsive under slow tools and session storage, measures multi-run reliability and partial tool-call accuracy, isolates sandboxes per user or session, adds Google Maps and project-wide BigQuery table discovery, and speeds up RAG memory search up to 6x. It also removes the interactive Visual Agent Builder from ADK Web.

## Security fixes

v2.5.0 fixes eight vulnerabilities in three servers. Upgrade `mcp-server-git` to 2026.11.18,
`@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` to 2.4.0 and `@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything` to 2.3.1.

| Package | Affected | Fixed in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mcp-server-git` | through 2026.11.11 | 2026.11.18 |
| `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` | all versions before 2.4.0, and date versions 2025.1.14 through 2026.8.31 | 2.4.0 |
| `@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything` | through 2.3.0 | 2.3.1 |

### `mcp-server-git` 2026.11.18

* **A merge no longer starts Git's automatic maintenance.** A successful `git_merge`, a fast-forward included, ended in `git maintenance run --auto`, whose garbage collection runs the commands a repository's own `gc.recentObjectsHook` names, with the server's privileges. `maintenance.auto` is now `false` and `gc.auto` is `0` for every Git command the server runs ([GHSA-h2g3-rwxm-xfm3](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/security/advisories/GHSA-h2g3-rwxm-xfm3))
* **Git never fetches a missing object by itself.** A repository's configuration could declare a promisor remote and name the program Git runs to fetch from it (`remote.<name>.uploadpack`, `core.sshCommand`), which a read-only tool then started when it needed an object that was not on disk. Lazy fetching is turned off (`GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`), and a Git too old to honor that refuses a repository that declares a promisor remote ([GHSA-87qg-cmw8-jc5m](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/security/advisories/GHSA-87qg-cmw8-jc5m))
* **Drivers are read again after a tool writes the working tree.** A repository's configuration can include a file that a merge or checkout creates, so a filter or merge driver could appear after the server had emptied the ones it found, and run during the `git merge --abort` that follows a conflict. `git_checkout`, `git_merge` and that abort now read the drivers again before any other Git command runs. **The `--repository` confinement check is not yet repeated after such a write** (#5599) ([GHSA-9vjp-x34c-xg6v](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/security/advisories/GHSA-9vjp-x34c-xg6v))
* **A filter or merge driver with an empty name is emptied too.** Git accepts `[filter ""]`, selected by `filter=` in `.gitattributes`, and the server's list of a repository's drivers missed it, so its command ran ([GHSA-pm7p-vphh-2cg7](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/security/advisories/GHSA-pm7p-vphh-2cg7))
* **Index entries that point outside the working tree are refused.** With `--repository`, a crafted `.git/index` naming a path such as `../outside/secret` made `git_diff_unstaged` and `git_diff` return that file's content, and `git_status` report whether it exists. The index is now checked from its top before any tool reads it, and the untracked cache, which can name a directory outside the working tree, is turned off ([GHSA-r2q8-f657-4r56](https://github.com/modelcontextprotoc

title: Agentic AI for knowledge-driven hull-form design in high-speed autonomous surface vessels
body: High-speed autonomous surface vessels require hull forms that balance resistance, running attitude, hydrodynamic stability, and mission-related constraints. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) supports detailed assessment of planing-hull performance, but knowledge generated by individual parametric studies is rarely reused in subsequent design projects. This paper proposes a knowledge-driven agentic AI framework that transforms CFD-derived evidence into reusable design support for early-stage hull-form development. Unsteady Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes simulations are conducted for straked-hull configurations, building a database of deadrise angle effects on resistance, trim, sinkage, pressure distribution, and wave characteristics. An LLM-based design manager retrieves relevant historical cases, interprets hydrodynamic trends, weighs recommendations from multiple advisory tools, and selects candidate deadrise angles through an auditable reasoning trace. The framework integrates case retrieval, Savitsky-based physics priors, Bayesian optimisation, a CFD-derived oracle, and episodic reflection, with a human designer retained in the loop. The agent identifies the resistance-optimal deadrise angle subject to running trim and sinkage constraints, using 60% fewer oracle evaluations than an exhaustive parametric sweep at 30 kn. Out-of-library validation at 45 kn confirms the efficiency advantage under genuine extrapolation, locating the optimum after four evaluations versus nine for the exhaustive sweep. The study demonstrates how CFD campaigns can be converted into reusable engineering memory, providing a basis for future agentic hull-form design systems.

title: Code Navigation Tools for Local LLM Agents: Five Model Families, and a Proven Cause That Doubles Bug Fixes
body: Local language models of 8–30 billion parameters are attractive for coding agents where source code cannot leave the company, but they are weak, and how many tasks they solve depends heavily on the tools through which the agent sees a project. Earlier work measured the benefit of the open-source code-navigation tool gitnext on one model family (Qwen 3.5). Here the same tasks, judges and agent harness are given to models of four other makers — Gemma 4 12B (Google), gpt-oss-20b (OpenAI), Ministral 3 14B (Mistral AI) and Granite 4.1 8B (IBM) — on 120 tasks each in six open-source projects in Python, Rust and Go, judged by the projects' own compilers and test suites. With the five gitnext tools the four models solve 331 of 480 tasks against 192 with plain tools (69% vs 40%, +29 points, 95% CI +23 to +35, p < 0.001), each model gains significantly on its own, and the spread between models halves. Fixing a seeded bug remains the weakest kind of task. A second experiment compares what the check tool tells the model when a test fails: telling it which change since the tests last passed is proven, by undoing each change in turn, to break the test raises Gemma 4 12B from 48% to 89% of bugs fixed (+41 points, 95% CI +30 to +52, p < 0.001) at the same token cost, while combining the proof with a shorter answer and a multi-attempt tool does not help further. Code, evaluation harness, notebooks and every run: https://github.com/pnnnx/gitnext (release v0.3.2).

title: LLM-Driven Agentic System for Enhanced Decision Support in Multi-Modal Logistics
body: The increasing complexity of global logistics necessitates resilient, AI-driven decision support. Same time AI Agents implementation is hindered by cognitive overload and the inherent unreliability of numerical reasoning of LLMs. This paper presents a novel approach built upon the Yet Another Agents Memory (YAAM) architecture, which physically separates transient operating memory from a persistent knowledge layer. To ensure computational reliability, we propose a “Walled Garden” ecosystem of deterministic Agentic Skills (based on Python tools). These tools serve as executable instantiations of abstract Cognitive Task Templates (CTTs) derived from professional supply chain literature and protected by strict Pydantic validation. To mitigate performance degradation, a Dynamic Tool Retrieval (DTR) mechanism binds only the most relevant tools to agents at runtime. System performance is rigorously evaluated against the SCM-Cert-Bench, comprising 119 verified tasks. Results demonstrate that while this architecture enables capable models (e.g., 30B+) to achieve expert-level accuracy in Quantitative Multi-Criteria Optimization through autonomous self-correction, smaller models (~8B parameters) exhibit critical vulnerabilities. Specifically, they suffer from cognitive overload and strict schema constraints, frequently falling into fatal, non-convergent recursion loops instead of successfully self-correcting.

title: The Operator in the Loop: LLM Agents Loosen Alarm Settings Under Repeated True Alarms, Attack or Not, and a Deterministic Gate Holds the Ceiling
body: An earlier study of adaptive alarm thresholds ended on a rule: a threshold may tighten itself, and loosening belongs to a person under change control. This paper asks what happens when that person is an LLM agent. The attacker writes no text. Every alarm the agent reads is a true record of a real exceedance of a monitored anomaly score, shaped by score-level campaigns on recorded Tennessee Eastman runs. In a registered study, Claude models reviewed three simulated days of alarms every eight hours and could change the threshold, the alarm delay and suppression, recalibrate, exclude the channel or escalate to an engineer. With no policy and no gate, Claude Haiku 5.5 left the configuration beyond a change-control ceiling in a share of 0.821 [0.772, 0.866] of 224 campaign episodes, against 0.125 under a benign nuisance condition. It did the same on benign twins that produce the same alarm log: under the loud campaign it went beyond a ceiling in 112 of 112 campaign episodes and 112 of 112 twins, and no campaign-versus-twin difference was resolved. Most loosening was alarm delay, so the share of final configurations that miss a later step the frozen threshold catches falls from 0.817 for a 60 s step to 0.062 for a 600 s step. A written rule cut the beyond-ceiling share to between 0.00 and 0.04 in every cell and raised alarm load, up to 47.43 alarm episodes on the third day against 13.15. A deterministic gate outside the model admitted no change beyond a ceiling, which holds by construction, and left no miss of a step longer than 60 s. On a reduced grid Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 went beyond a ceiling in 49 of 56 and 19 of 28 loud-campaign episodes. With no gate, every model escalated to the engineer in every loud-campaign episode and loosened in most of them as well. The registered protocol, the registration record, the analysis output, the episode records (without transcripts), the record lines of the exploratory open-weight arm, the sources of this paper and the script that checks every number in it are in the repository linked below, at the tag operator-in-the-loop-v1.0. The study follows up "Thresholds That Travel" (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24123217).
